body: Tibetan, spoken by some seven million people on and around the Qinghai-Xizang Plateau, remains underrepresented in natural language processing (NLP). We present, to our knowledge, the first peer-reviewed systematic bibliometric survey of Tibetan NLP: 140 publications from 2004 to 2026 in the ACL Anthology and DBLP, annotated for venue type, research area, first-affiliation country, and resource release. Output has grown rapidly, with 84% of the publications appearing since 2018, and has expanded bottom-up along the NLP pipeline, from corpora and word segmentation through script, speech, and applications to large language models (LLMs). Researchers based in China first-authored 87% of the publications, which span all 25 represented research areas, whereas work from other countries concentrates on Classical Tibetan. We argue that this full-pipeline paradigm, realized under the compounded constraints of a complex script, dialectal diversity, and geographic remoteness, offers a reference model for other low-resource languages of the Global South. We also identify gaps in dialect coverage, responsible NLP, native and comparable evaluation, cross-community visibility, and resource release (only 29% of the publications release data, code, or models), and recommend open science, shared standards, and community participation for the LLM era.
summaryZh: 本文对2004年至2026年间的藏语自然语言处理（NLP）研究进行了首次同行评审的系统性文献计量调查。研究分析了140篇相关文献，指出藏语NLP研究在过去几年中增长迅速，且已形成从语料库到大语言模型（LLM）的全流程范式。尽管中国研究者在其中占据主导地位，但该领域仍面临 dialectal diversity（方言多样性）和资源匮乏的挑战。文章建议通过开放科学与社区协作，推动低资源语言在LLM时代的进一步发展。
